entries.content: N-BaIoT introductory paper: arXiv:1805.03409v1 preprint, 8-page PDF. Related published article: IEEE Pervasive Computing, vol. 17, no. 3, pp. 12-22, 2018, article 8490192, DOI: 10.1109/MPRV.2018.03367731. The arXiv v1 PDF itself carries an incorrect VOL. 13, NO. 9 header; that header is not used as final bibliographic metadata. Table 2 and the 'Feature extraction' section define 23 features per time scale over four aggregation objects (Source IP, Source MAC-IP, Channel, Socket), which resolves the MI_dir_* prefix by elimination: MI_dir = Source MAC-IP aggregation (weight=damped count; mean/variance=mean and variance of outbound-only packet sizes). The literal string 'MI_dir' does not appear in the paper text.
entries.usage: Derived-evidence source for the N-BaIoT MI_dir_* semantic disposition; recorded as derived, not exact, because the prefix attribution is by elimination from group widths

entries.content: Official UNB CICIoT2023 dataset page snapshot: states 33 attacks in 7 categories (DDoS, DoS, Recon, Web-based, Brute Force, Spoofing, Mirai) and places Backdoor malware under Web-based, ARP/DNS spoofing under Spoofing, Dictionary brute force under Brute Force. The page's own category detail lists enumerate 32 attacks: the DDoS list has 11 entries and omits DDoS-ICMP_Fragmentation, which IS present in the frozen dataset directories and in README.pdf. The formal enumeration baseline is the frozen inventory directories plus README.pdf; the 32/33 page discrepancy is recorded here as an official-source inconsistency.
entries.usage: Official classification source for the CICIoT2023 type-mapping proposal; also records the UNB page 32/33 enumeration inconsistency and the resolution baseline (frozen directories + README.pdf)

entries.content: README.pdf page-1 47-row feature table (rows 1-47: ts, flow duration, Header Length, Protocol Type, Duration, Rate, Srate, Drate, flags 9-15, flag counts 16-20, HTTP/HTTPS/DNS/Telnet/SMTP/SSH/IRC 21-27, TCP/UDP 28-29, DHCP/ARP/ICMP/IPv/LLC 30-34, Tot sum/Min/Max/AVG/Std 35-39, Tot size/IAT/Number 40-42, Magnitue/Radius/Covariance/Variance/Weight 43-47; original spellings preserved verbatim incl. 'urg coun', 'Magnitue', 'Drate,'). Key protocol rows: 28 TCP 'Indicates if the transport layer protocol is TCP'; 29 UDP 'Indicates if the transport layer protocol is UDP'; 32 ICMP 'Indicates if the network layer protocol is ICMP'; 35 Tot sum 'Summation of packets lengths in flow'. In this table every listed feature is a per-flow indicator or aggregate (0/1 indicator semantics implied by 'Indicates if').
entries.usage: Official page-1 feature-semantics evidence for the CICIoT2023 protocol-indicator columns, per the #23 Rev 1 independent-review requirement (the page-2 attack-category panels do not document feature semantics). NOTE: README.pdf page 1 embeds TWO feature tables with CONFLICTING protocol semantics; this is the 47-row indicator-style table, and both tables are recorded as an official-source internal inconsistency.

entries.content: README.pdf page-1 39-row window-aggregation feature table (rows 1-39: Header Length, Time-To-Live, Rate, flags 4-10, flag counts 11-14, IGMP/HTTPS/HTTP/Telnet/DNS/SMTP/SSH/IRC 15-22, TCP/UDP/DHCP/ARP/ICMP/IPv/LLC 23-29, Tot Sum/Min/Max/AVG/Std 30-34, Tot Size/IAT/Number 35-37, Variance 38, Protocol Type 39). Key protocol rows: 23 TCP 'Average no. of TCP packets in the window'; 24 UDP 'Average no. of UDP packets in the window'; 27 ICMP 'Average no. of ICMP packets in the window'; 30 Tot Sum 'Total packet length within the aggregated packets (window)'. This table describes window-aggregate semantics ('Average no. of ... packets in the window') for the same protocol names that the 47-row table describes as per-flow 0/1-style indicators.
entries.usage: Second official page-1 feature-semantics source for the CICIoT2023 protocol-indicator columns. Together with the 47-row table this constitutes an OFFICIAL-SOURCE INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY about the semantics of the protocol indicator columns; this inconsistency is one of the grounds for keeping all cross-dataset protocol mappings out of admission in #23 Rev 1 (dataset-native remains the mainline; tcp/udp stay candidates; no seven-gate pass is claimed).
